title: Delegated break-glass, KMS dual-control & SSO forensics PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Define and deliver a production-ready PRD for delegated emergency (break-glass) access, KMS dual-control workflows, and SSO/SAML assertion provenance + session forensics requirements for Private/VPC deployments. Scope covers requirements, acceptance criteria, test plan, logging schema, evidence artifacts for audits, and a sign-off checklist for product, security, legal, and SRE.

Background: Several enterprise customers asked for stronger emergency-access controls and forensic evidence for operator actions in private deployments. Existing sign-off playbooks focus on SSO, RBAC, and KMS separately; this PRD unifies: (a) controlled break-glass that leaves tamper-evident traces, (b) dual-control KMS operations for high-sensitivity keys, and (c) SAML assertion provenance and session forensic telemetry to support post-incident reviews and audits.

Non-goals: Building a full BYOK UI for key import (we will integrate with existing KMS/Bring-Your-Own-Key flows) and creating a separate identity provider. This PRD focuses on evidence, workflows, and automation hooks for operator tooling and auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Break-glass initiation must require two independent approvals: an automated policy check and one live human approver; both approvals are recorded as immutable audit entries.

All break-glass actions must emit an auditable bundle: user IDs, SAML assertion ID, assertion fingerprint, timestamp (UTC), origin IP, session id, and a signed event digest stored in customer audit logs and Redwood control plane (where allowed).

KMS dual-control operations (key unseal, emergency decrypt) must require quorum of two operator roles; operations generate an HSM/KMS audit record and a correlated Redwood event with a stable correlation id.

SAML assertion provenance: the platform must persist assertion metadata (issuer, subject, audience, assertion_id, signature_verification_result) for the lifetime of the session and surface this in session forensics exports.

Session forensics export must support two formats: (1) compressed JSONL for internal analysis; (2) signed tarball (with manifest) for regulator evidence packages. Exports include request/response hashes, model_id, route, tokens_issued, and latency percentiles per route for the session window.

RBAC mappings for delegated break-glass must be auditable and reversible; role elevation requests are recorded and automatically expire after configurable TTL with a follow-up review task created for compliance teams.
End-to-end automated tests covering happy path, denial path, and failure modes (network interruptions during approval) must exist in ENG and pass in CI prior to release.
signoff_checklist: Product sign-off: PM confirms scope and acceptance criteria documented (Aisha Kapoor)
Security sign-off: Threat model, mitigation backlog, and SSO/KMS cryptographic validation (lead: Priya Menon)
SRE sign-off: Runbook, rollback, and alerting thresholds validated (lead: Ben Carter)
Legal/compliance sign-off: Evidence package format acceptable for SOC2 and customer audits (legal reviewer: Elena Novak)
UX/Docs sign-off: User-facing break-glass flows and admin docs published (owner: UX writer)
Operator training sign-off: Internal runthrough completed and recording uploaded
Operational readiness: Canary test in dedicated environment with synthetic workload and audit ingestion verified
test_plan: Unit + integration tests for assertion fingerprinting and signature verification (ENG PR #5421)
Chaos test: simulate approval service latency and validate that pending approvals are quiesced and logged (SRE test harness)
Dual-control KMS test: simulate two operators performing emergency decrypt, verify KMS audit trail and correlation id mapping in control plane
Export validation: generate regulator package and run automated schema validator (contrib script: tools/forensics-validate.py)
E2E: full break-glass flow initiated via Console, approvals via SSO IdP, action executed, and evidence exported to customer S3

2025-11-18: Security review (initial) — request to include signed event digest to mitigate tampering; added to acceptance criteria; follow-up: crypto team to review HSM signing approach (PRD v1.1).

2025-12-09: Design feedback — prefer inline confirmation modal in Console for break-glass with copy explaining audit retention. UX to supply copy by 2026-01-05. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/breakglass-ux-draft
2026-01-22: ENG spike completed — validated KMS dual-control using existing HSM operator roles; draft implementation plan in GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-kms/pull/314

2026-01-30: Compliance asked for signed tarball format for regulator exports; added export manifest requirement and schema. Reference: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/Forensics+Export+Schema

2026-02-02: Trade-off noted: requiring two human approvers increases MTTR during legit emergencies. Mitigation: allow timed auto-approval if SLOs are breached AND an encrypted escrow key is used; requires explicit customer opt-in. Added to non-goals unless customer enables.
